summary: In New York, a person aged 14 to 17 generally needs an employment certificate, called working papers, to work.
realLife: In New York, 14- to 17-year-olds generally need an employment certificate, issued by school officials, with proof of age and a doctor's exam.
sources: New York State Department of Labor, Working Papers: https://dol.ny.gov/working-papers
inGame: the person's age at the hire row and the state's child labor rules. needs: a work permit on a minor's hire.

turns.what: A job in an exempt kind of work, such as babysitting or farm work, with no papers.
A first job after 18, when no papers are needed.
